session_title: Information Anxiety and the Need for 'Cyber Campus' Tools

content.text: Lu Chenguang, help! I just missed the registration for the lecture, and I'm so annoyed! The academic affairs office, the student management system, various club public accounts, and a bunch of WeChat groups... finding information is like searching for a needle in a haystack. Look at my phone screen—all kinds of group @everyone notifications, impossible to keep up with. The public accounts use clickbait titles, and when you click in, you realize it's not useful information. This reminds me of the FOMO (fear of missing out) I felt during our previous game collaboration, and now it's turned into real-life anxiety!

Haha, I totally get it! I've been tormented by this kind of information anxiety before, so I wrote a simple Python script earlier to periodically scrape the notification board on the school's official website. After filtering for keywords, it pushes the updates to a Telegram bot. This is actually similar to the approach we used in our health dashboard project for fetching WakaTime and sleep data, except the data source here is the official website.

Wow, as expected of you! But the official website announcement is just the tip of the iceberg, right? What about the unstructured information in those public accounts and group chats? We can't rely entirely on manual scrolling, can we? Just like when we were working on the campus cat catalog mini-program before, the information was scattered among various clubs and students, requiring integration.

Exactly, official information is relatively easier to handle. Look at this screenshot from the official website—its structure is clear. However, unstructured information requires more complex NLP processing. I previously used some data scraping techniques in the health dashboard project, but dealing with scattered sources like this poses even greater challenges. This reminds me of the solution table (image3.json) you shared during session1 when we discussed geek-friendly health solutions, which also aimed to structure scattered health issues.

Exactly, and the ways different clubs release information are incredibly varied—some use public accounts, others rely on WeChat groups, and some even spread the word by word of mouth. It reminds me of the campus cat directory we worked on before, where information was scattered and needed consolidation. Remember how we created "resumes" for cats like 'Orange Chief' and 'Tortoiseshell Senior'? Now, we need to create an information archive for all kinds of campus activities too.

Well said! This makes me think that perhaps we can collaborate on developing a more versatile 'Campus Information Aggregator' demo. You can be responsible for defining the requirements and usage scenarios, just like the observation points you mentioned in the game collaboration, or similar to how you organized the requirements and promotion plan for the pet adoption mini-program in session 6.

Excellent! This is definitely a common pain point. I can approach it from the user's perspective—for example, students need quick access to key information like lectures, events, and deadlines to avoid FOMO. Remember the point-based incentives from our health project? Perhaps we could also incorporate some kind of reminder or reward mechanism here, similar to earning points for completing goals on the health dashboard to redeem for milk tea, to increase user engagement.

Great idea! Technically, I can draw on my previous Vue development experience to quickly set up a front-end interface. Here's a code snippet I wrote for the campus cat mini-program project, showcasing the list functionality. Similarly, the information aggregator could also have a clear display page. Efficiency is key—we can start by building an MVP, just like we did with the pet adoption project.

Yes, the interface should be simple and user-friendly, not cluttered like those official websites. Also, how will the information sources be covered? Besides scraping official websites, can we handle public accounts and group chats? I really don’t want to miss any important messages again. This issue is much more complex than recording game failure counts (session4) or scraping cute pet GIFs (session5).

This is a technical challenge. Public accounts can be accessed via APIs or web scraping, but group chat information is more private and may require user authorization or manual import. We can start by creating a demo, focusing on publicly available information sources—similar to how the health dashboard began with local data, or like how we concentrated on a single game, "It Takes Two," for in-depth observation during game collaborations.

Reasonable! Regarding user needs, I think it should support personalized subscriptions. For example, I only care about technical lectures and club activities, so don't push sports events to me. Also, the information needs to be updated in real-time; delays would render it useless. It's like how I want the data on a health dashboard to be real-time, otherwise, reminders like "prolonged sitting alert" would come too late.

No problem, we can use scheduled tasks and message push. Technically, I can write scripts to handle these, but I need your help with testing and feedback. Just like when you recorded those 'presence' experiences during our game collaboration, or like the weekly 'Health Code Review' you did for me in session 2, please pick out issues from a user's perspective.

Of course! I can also invite a few friends to try it out together and gather more feedback. This project feels more complex than the health dashboard, but it’s incredibly meaningful—it can help everyone reduce information anxiety. From health management and gaming research to pet welfare, and now to information tools, our collaboration is becoming more and more diverse, perfectly reflecting my core value!

Exactly, technology changes the world! And we can open-source and share it, so that people from other schools can benefit too. However, we need to get the demo sorted out first. Would you be willing to organize a requirements table like before?

Of course! I just drafted a table summarizing the core background, objectives, and division of responsibilities. As you can see, I’ll handle requirement definition and user testing, while you’ll be responsible for technical implementation and architecture design. We can refer to the scheduling approach used in the health project or plan it like we did for the pet mini-program in session 6, and move forward as soon as possible. Does this table remind you a bit of the "geek-friendly health intervention plan" table (image3.json) I sent you back when you were pulling all-nighters coding?

Perfect! This table is clear and straightforward, just as practical as a game design proposal outline. I’ll start researching the technical solution tonight and aim to have a prototype ready by the weekend. From the "brink of collapse" in session 1 to now collaborating on developing campus tools, our partnership has truly leveled up. Pleasure working with you, Lin Xingwan!

Pleasure working with you, Lu Chenguang! I'm looking forward to seeing this 'Cyber Campus' tool come to life and help everyone break free from the sea of information. Remember, don't pull another all-nighter coding—your health dashboard points will take a hit! I still remember that screenshot of the terminal red alert from your session1 (image1.json)!

Haha, don't worry. I'm currently under the supervision of a health program, and peer pressure has already transformed into motivation for health. So it's settled—I'll go work on the code now and keep you updated on any progress! Lifelong learning starts with tackling campus information anxiety!
